title: panic: Char index out of bounds
body:
### Summary

```
thread 'main' panicked at C:\Users\<user>/.cargo\registry\src\index.crates.io-6f17d22bba15001f\ropey-1.6.1\src\slice.rs:360:41:
called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: Char index out of bounds: char index 88087, Rope/RopeSlice char length 10230
```

### Reproduction Steps

<!-- Ideally provide a key sequence and/or asciinema.org recording. --> 

I tried this:

Panic occurred during selection over many lines. I clicked and dragged with mouse across about 20 lines and was intending to press "s" to select a specific word. I do not know if I had already clicked s or not when the panic happened.

I expected this to happen:

No panic

Instead, this happened:

Panic


### Helix log

Dunno where this file is on Windows, no such ~/.cache dir



### Platform

Windows

### Terminal Emulator

alacritty 0.15.1 (0c405d5)

### Installation Method

scoop

### Helix Version

helix 25.01.1 (e7ac2fcd)

comments.author: participant11
comments.body:
In case this is helpful to anyone experiencing crashes: [`asciinema`](https://asciinema.org/) lets you record all terminal input to figure out what led up to it. I had a very intermittent crash but was able to get the report in https://github.com/helix-editor/helix/issues/12582#issuecomment-4107545760 by defining a wrapper so Helix was always launched via asciinema. With nushell:

```nu
def --wrapped hx [...x] {
    let name = $"($env.HOME)/.cache/recordings/helix-(date now | format date "%Y-%m-%d_%H%M%S").cast"
    RUST_BACKTRACE=full asciinema rec --command $"hx ($x | str join ' ')" $name
}
```

For Bash it's probably easiest to create `~/.local/bin/hx` (assuming that's in your path) with contents like (untested)

```bash
#!/bin/sh

name="$HOME/.cache/recordings/helix-$(date "+%Y-%m-%d_%H%M%S").cast"
# warning! this simple solution may not work if Helix is passed file names
# containing spaces.
RUST_BACKTRACE=full asciinema rec --command "$name $*"
```

Those will create a report in `~/.cache/recordings/helix-*` (asciinema prints the full path when done). Whether or not the report is actually useful, I have no idea. But at least I can replay exactly what led up to the crash, rather than trying to remember what you were doing if it's not frequent.
